meta.title: API Trust-Boundary Confusion, OAuth2/PKCE & REST Differential Spectrum
meta.plainExplanation: Inspects API and authentication surfaces for X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP rate-limit and IP trust-boundary confusion, OAuth2/OIDC missing PKCE or deprecated grant types, and REST differential exposures.

meta.title: Web Cache Poisoning & Unkeyed Header Reflection (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Original-URL)
meta.plainExplanation: Probes an isolated cache-busted URL (?secscan_cb=<nonce>) with unkeyed forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Original-URL) and performs a clean follow-up request to verify whether the reflected header is stored in a shared HTTP cache.
meta.whyItMatters: If a reverse proxy or CDN caches a response containing an unkeyed header value, an attacker can poison the shared cache and serve malicious scripts or redirects to all visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.
meta.remediation: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.

meta.plainExplanation: Performs non-intrusive discovery and security auditing across Smart TVs (Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku ECP, Google TV / Android TV / Chromecast, Sony Bravia, Vizio SmartCast, Philips JointSpace, Apple AirPlay, DIAL), IP Cameras / NVRs (RTSP 554/8554, ONVIF SOAP, Hikvision ISAPI, Dahua, Axis, Xiongmai, UniFi Protect, unauthenticated snapshots), PCs / Workstations / Local Servers (Windows SMB/NetBIOS/MSRPC/RDP/WinRM/WSDAPI, macOS/Linux SSH/VNC/CUPS/NFS/AFP/rsync/mDNS, Docker TCP 2375, Ollama 11434, local dev servers, open shares), routers, printers, NAS, and IoT appliances.
meta.whyItMatters: Local network devices and workstations often expose unauthenticated REST/WebSocket control APIs, live RTSP/MJPEG camera feeds, cleartext admin UIs, unauthenticated Docker/Ollama/dev servers, or remote file-sharing and shell services (SMB 445, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985, ADB 5555, Telnet 23) that allow LAN attackers to hijack screens, view surveillance feeds, access files, or execute arbitrary commands.
meta.defaultFix: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.
meta.remediation: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.

meta.title: Universal Operating System, Edge Appliance & Market CVE Security Audit
meta.plainExplanation: Passively inspects HTTP headers, service banners, and open OS/appliance/runtime ports across Windows Server & Workstation, Linux distributions (Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky, Alpine), macOS / Apple Darwin / AirPlay, BSD / Firewall OS (FreeBSD, OpenBSD, pfSense, OPNsense), Edge VPN/Firewall/Router/NAS appliances (Palo Alto PAN-OS, Fortinet FortiOS, Ivanti Connect Secure, Citrix NetScaler, Cisco IOS XE, MikroTik RouterOS, QNAP QTS), and AI/Cloud runtimes (Ollama, Anyscale Ray) for End-of-Life OS releases and high-impact CVEs.

meta.remediation: Upgrade End-of-Life operating systems to actively supported LTS releases, upgrade OpenSSH to 9.9p2+ (or apply vendor backport security updates), restrict or disable CUPS (631), AirPlay (5000/7000), SMB (445), and RDP (3389) on untrusted networks, apply emergency patches for PAN-OS, FortiOS, Ivanti, Citrix NetScaler, Cisco IOS XE, MikroTik RouterOS, and QNAP QTS appliances, and upgrade Ollama to 0.1.34+ and Ray to 2.8.1+ while binding AI runtimes to localhost.

meta.title: PHP session.upload_progress LFI-to-RCE & Serializer Mismatch (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)
meta.plainExplanation: Passively and safely inspects PHP targets for the php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) session.upload_progress multipart PHPSESSID fixation, raw filename session injection, var_destroy UAF, and FPM PS(serializer) handler mismatch conditions.
meta.whyItMatters: In PHP 5.4.0 through 8.5.11, the rfc1867 session.upload_progress handler accepts PHPSESSID from multipart POST form data ignoring session.use_only_cookies and writes raw filenames into session files, enabling LFI-to-RCE and deserialization RCE.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.
meta.remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.

meta.remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.

findings.name: Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA) on Menu/Form Endpoint
findings.detail: Menu "Main Menu -> Features" (/en/features) was discovered during authenticated crawling but returned HTTP 200 content when probed without session cookies or Authorization headers (unauthenticated BFLA).
findings.fix: Enforce server-side authentication and role-based access control (RBAC) middleware on all administrative menu views, SPA templates, and form action endpoints. Deny unauthenticated and unauthorized low-privilege requests with HTTP 401/403.

meta.title: API BOLA / IDOR & Mass Assignment Privilege Attribute Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Inspects REST API object endpoints (/api/users/1) against a non-existent canary route to detect unauthenticated Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) and checks whether privilege-escalation fields (role, isAdmin, is_superuser) are exposed.
meta.whyItMatters: Broken Object Level Authorization (OWASP API1:2023) allows attackers to read or modify other users’ records by enumerating IDs, while Mass Assignment allows binding privileged fields like role or isAdmin.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce object-level ownership checks on every record lookup, use non-sequential UUIDs, and restrict request body deserialization to explicit allowlisted DTO fields.
meta.remediation: Enforce object-level ownership checks on every record lookup, use non-sequential UUIDs, and restrict request body deserialization to explicit allowlisted DTO fields.

findings.remediation: Enforce server-side authentication and role-based access control (RBAC) middleware on all administrative menu views, SPA templates, and form action endpoints. Deny unauthenticated and unauthorized low-privilege requests with HTTP 401/403.
